t: In the event of any conflict between the requirements of orders or regulations issued by the Secretary under this title and title I of this Act applicable to motor vehicle tires and orders or administrative interpretations issued by the Federal Trade Commission, the provisions of orders or regulations issued by the Secretary shall prevail.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the mention of "regulations issued by the Secretary" signals rulemaking and so participation. But this section does not grant or require rulemaking; it only sets a precedence rule for conflicts between the Secretary's orders or regulations and those of the Federal Trade Commission. Both actors are inside the federal government, and no outside party is consulted, heard, or given a right to sue.
fable.s: the provisions of orders or regulations issued by the Secretary shall prevail

qwen_block.w: This section establishes a hierarchy of authority between two federal agencies (the Secretary and the Federal Trade Commission) in the event of a regulatory conflict. It does not involve consultation, coordination, or participation with any party outside the federal government. The interaction is purely intra-governmental.
qwen_block.s: In the event of any conflict between the requirements of orders or regulations issued by the Secretary under this title and title I of this Act applicable to motor vehicle tires and orders or administrative interpretations issued by the Federal Trade Commission, the provisions of orders or regulations issued by the Secretary shall prevail.

opus.w: This provision only decides which rule controls when the Secretary's rules and the Federal Trade Commission's rules conflict. That is a matter between two federal agencies. It does not grant or require any new rulemaking, comment period, hearing, consultation or right to sue. The mention of 'regulations' is tempting, but the text only refers to regulations issued under other provisions; it does not authorize them, so the rulemaking rule from the examples does not apply.
opus.s: In the event of any conflict between the requirements of orders or regulations issued by the Secretary under this title and title I of this Act applicable to motor vehicle tires and orders or administrative interpretations issued by the Federal Trade Commission, the provisions of orders or regulations issued by the Secretary shall prevail.
opus.b:
1. **Thinking it through.** The tempting reading is "Yes", because the section mentions "orders or regulations issued by the Secretary". The examples count a grant of rulemaking authority as participation. But this section does not grant, require or authorize any new rulemaking. It only says which rule wins when the Secretary's existing orders or regulations conflict with the Federal Trade Commission's. Both of those are federal agencies, and no outside party is consulted or given a role.
